question.text: A pendulum clock (fitted with a small heavy bob that is connected with a metal rod) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> seconds fast each day at a temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> seconds slow at a temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Find the temperature (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>) at which it will show the correct time.

solution.text:
Fractional loss of time per second =12αΔT

Therefore 12αT0−15×(24hrs)=3

and 12α30−T0×(24hrs)=2
on solving T0=24°C
